cards.result: The spiral tower is in the game (commit 5bba87c): a 4×4 building outside that opens to a 2×2 room inside, with a wall, a doorway and a wider view of the farm behind it, and saves and reloads correctly. Tests and screenshots came with it. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

The three integration tests that failed on CI but passed on our machines now wait for the right thing (commit 7618844): the coop test waits for the ground to be ready, the window test counts only the player's own actions, and the cot test times itself in game time instead of by the wall clock. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

The game now keeps three separate save slots, and the nine developer tools that start the game play on a scratch slot of their own instead of the player's farm (commit 7e4e66e), so running a tool can no longer overwrite a real save. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

cards.reason: Built on main, following Daniel's ruling on Q-88.
cards.result: The first robot now unlocks after a day of watering and the second after the first robot finishes its first job (commit 35714f2). The shop shows each only once it is earned, and saves and replays remember the unlock, including on older saves. This follows Daniel's ruling on Q-88; an automated check passed on the work, but no checker or Daniel approval was recorded for this close.

The simulation speed test's old target, 100,000 times real time, was a round number with nothing behind it. Commit c8fa853 replaces it with a target taken from what the game actually asks of the simulation each frame, plus a cheap alarm for a large slowdown (decision S-15). No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

When the Animation Lab redraws a loop, it now compares the values the script actually used against the ones that were asked for, and says which script ignored its settings instead of reporting a redraw that changed nothing. This is in hq/anim.py as it landed in commit d417023. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

The sprite catalog now marks the sheets that hold separate pictures rather than an animation (the sprinkler, soil, obstacles and the mole), so previews stop playing them as if they moved (commit 804867d). Two checks came with it: every frame lies inside its sheet, and every animation points at frames that exist. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.

The design note on how a robot is earned rather than bought is in docs/design/06-bots-and-training.md (commit f2e821a): the first robot is earned by a day of watering, the second by the first robot's first job, following Daniel's ruling on Q-88. The decision log and the designer queue record it. No checker or Daniel approval was recorded.
